reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) demonstrates that adjusting V, Ti, Nb ratios and annealing introduces multi-phase structures and improves strength-ductility synergy in V-Ti-Cr-Nb-Mo RHEAs. However, the evidence is from a different alloy system (containing Cr and Mo) and does not test high-temperature mechanical properties (only room temperature compression is reported). The premise that these principles apply to TiVNbTa at 1273 K is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Adjusting elemental ratios in RHEAs can introduce multi-phase microstructures (e.g., BCC+HCP+Laves)
Heat treatments can modify phase fractions and morphology in RHEAs
Multi-phase microstructures enhance strength-ductility synergy in RHEAs
These principles apply to the TiVNbTa alloy system
